first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this with 'It's Santorini, Mum, it's decided.' Well, the first paragraph agrees with her and then gets straight to the order of things: legal or symbolic, season, guest list, documents, rules. No 'dreamy' this or 'magical' that. Nine steps and a checklist. I'll read it top to bottom with a cup of tea.

journey.section: Step 1: Decide between a legal and a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: A symbolic ceremony on the island, after a legal step at home, keeps the paperwork in Australia and frees the day itself.
journey.reaction: That's what I'll be suggesting. Sign at the registry in Melbourne, then enjoy the island without Greek forms. Good that it's put as a proper option and not a second-best.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but it may not work as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: I'd never have thought of that. She'll want to change her name on her passport. Useful, and plainly said.

journey.section: Weather by month from official station data
journey.quote: The figures below are for Naxos, the nearest official station, so read them as a guide to the neighbourhood rather than a forecast for the caldera.
journey.reaction: Honest. The table is a lot of numbers on the iPad, but the paragraph after it tells me what they mean, so I skipped to that.

journey.section: Heat, wind and wildfire advice for travellers
journey.quote: Plan water, light fabrics, shade and air-conditioned rest for guests, and set a summer ceremony later in the day.
journey.reaction: Mum doesn't manage heat. Air-conditioned rest is exactly the phrase I wanted to see. Someone has thought about the older guests, not just the photos.

journey.section: Heat, wind and wildfire advice for travellers
journey.quote: Neither is a reason to look elsewhere, but both are reasons to keep travel insurance in place for everyone travelling.
journey.reaction: Earthquakes and a volcano. I'd rather know than not. And travel insurance for everyone, which I'll be nagging the whole family about anyway. Calm, not alarming.

journey.section: Step 4: Size your guest list against capacity and rooms
journey.quote: The caldera-edge spaces in Oia and Imerovigli seat between 15 and 60.
journey.reaction: Fifteen to sixty. Our side alone is forty. So it's the winery or splitting things up, or someone's being left off the list. That's a conversation I need to have before anyone pays anything, and I'm glad I know now.

journey.section: Step 4: Size your guest list against capacity and rooms
journey.quote: | Katikies Chromata, Pool Bar area | Imerovigli | 40 to 50 | 50 |
journey.reaction: Thirteen rows, four columns, and I had to scroll sideways. Too many hotel names to keep straight. I'll let my husband print it.

journey.section: Step 5: Plan travel for your guests
journey.quote: Guests flying from Australia arrive tired, and some will be older or less steady on stairs.
journey.reaction: Thank you. That's Mum, and my aunt. First article I've read that says it out loud without making me feel I'm being fussy.

journey.quote: In most cases you carry your own luggage up and down stairs on ferries.
journey.reaction: Then Mum flies. That settles that. Practical detail like this is what I come for.

journey.section: Access and transfers to ask about
journey.quote: How far is the nearest point a car can reach, and how do guests with limited mobility get from there to the terrace?
journey.reaction: That is word for word my question. 'Can Mum with her walking frame get to the terrace?' I'll ask it of every one of them.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness.
journey.reaction: This part is long and dense: CNI, apostille, notary, authentication. I read it twice. It's thorough, but if they're doing the legal bit at home most of this won't apply, and I'd like to have been told I could skip it.

journey.section: Step 7: Lock in the house rules in writing
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Yes. Everything in writing. My husband will underline that. But in all these questions about music and suppliers, nobody asks about the deposit: how much, when, can we get it back, what if someone falls ill and the date moves.

journey.section: What shapes the cost of a Santorini wedding
journey.quote: At venues such as Grace Hotel, a wedding planner is required for every wedding, so their fee belongs in the plan from the start.
journey.reaction: Good to know before we budget. A cost that's compulsory and easy to miss. That's the kind of thing I want flagged.

journey.section: Plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, Australian dollars, fee in writing first. That's most of what I need from whoever we pay. I'd still want to talk to them on the phone before a cent goes anywhere.

unanswered_questions: What should we ask each venue about the deposit: how much, when it's due, whether it's refundable, and what happens if we need to move the date?
Are the venue contracts in English, and are they priced in euros?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Greek time?
If my daughter marries legally in Melbourne first, which parts of Step 6 can we ignore?
Is the first step with the Wedded Advisor a phone call, before anything is booked or paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: Before you sign with any venue, get written answers to each of these:
turn_offs_found.why: My turn-off is planning advice that never mentions deposits or who's responsible for the money. This checklist is otherwise excellent and I'll print it, but there are thirteen items and not one about the deposit, the payment schedule or cancellation. That's the first thing my husband will ask, and losing a deposit to an overseas supplier is the thing I'm most nervous about.

would_share_with: My husband, with the booking checklist printed and 'what about the deposit?' written at the bottom
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the heat, ferry stairs and access questions
My daughter, with the paragraph about signing legally at home and the name-change point

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: One person, my time zone, AUD, fee in writing. That's what I want. I'd click if I knew a real person would ring me first and could tell me straight which of these terraces Mum can actually reach.

top_3_changes: Add a deposit line to the Step 9 checklist and a matching question in Step 7: how much, when it's due, whether it's refundable and what happens if the date moves. It's the one money question the article never asks, and the first one a paying parent will.

At the top of Step 6, add one sentence saying couples who marry legally in Australia and hold a symbolic ceremony can skip most of this section, so readers on that path aren't wading through CNIs and apostilles.
Break up the Step 4 capacity table on mobile (for example group it by area, or keep the summary sentence above it) so it doesn't need sideways scrolling on an iPad.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad, mother uses a walking frame)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions only
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing, not-published lines and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: Deposit and cancellation is again absent from the venue questions and checklist; it can be added as a question to ask venues without new venue facts. Treat as should-fix? Contract language, on-the-day contact and a phone-first step are business details and deferred.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised. The deposit point concerns which question to ask venues, not a figure.
